html:
"Milano (Austria)" is the map's label, for 1783, for the Duchy of Milan under the rule of the Austrian Habsburgs, from 1714 to 1796.

Spain lost Milan to Austria after the War of the Spanish Succession. Under Maria Theresa and her son Joseph II the Habsburg monarchy reformed it: a land survey for fair taxes, fewer church privileges, and new schools. Milan became a centre of the Italian Enlightenment. Cesare Beccaria's book On Crimes and Punishments, published there in 1764, argued against torture and the death penalty and was read across Europe. La Scala opera house opened in 1778.

In 1796 Napoleon entered Milan and made it capital of a French client republic. Austria won it back in 1815 as part of Lombardy.
